source_note: Facts from the GitHub API on this date. Nothing here has been installed or run. Popularity is not quality.

items.name: yfinance
items.what: Downloads market data from Yahoo Finance.
items.fit: Already used by this dashboard for prices, dividends and holdings.
items.note: Unofficial: can break. That is why prices are cross-checked against the ASX.

items.name: PyPortfolioOpt
items.what: Works out how to split money across funds to balance risk and return.
items.fit: Useful later for a 'how much in each fund' suggestion.
items.note: Needs good return estimates; past returns are a weak guide, so treat output as a starting point.

items.name: QuantStats
items.what: Portfolio risk and return reports (drawdowns, volatility, Sharpe ratio).
items.fit: Overlaps what this dashboard already computes; could add polished report pages.

items.name: Riskfolio-Lib
items.what: Advanced portfolio optimisation and risk measures.
items.fit: More than you need for a few ETFs.
items.note: Powerful, but complexity can give false confidence.

items.name: ffn
items.fit: Same ground as the metrics already built.

items.name: Portfolio Performance
items.what: Desktop app to track what you own, performance, dividends and taxes.
items.fit: Good for tracking real holdings once you buy. This dashboard deliberately stores none of your holdings.
items.effort: Medium (install a desktop app; ask IT first)
items.verdict: Worth a look after you buy
items.note: Check how it handles Australian tax before relying on it.

items.name: Ghostfolio
items.what: Self-hosted wealth tracker with a web interface.
items.fit: Similar to this dashboard but tracks your holdings.
items.note: Docker needs IT sign-off, and holdings are personal data.

items.name: OpenBB
items.what: Open data platform for analysts, with many data sources and tools.
items.fit: Heavy; a data hub rather than an ETF dashboard.
items.note: Licence unclear. Check the terms before building on it.

items.name: vectorbt
items.what: Fast testing of trading strategies on past prices.
items.fit: Built for active trading, not buy-and-hold.
items.note: Backtests often look better than real results.

items.name: backtrader
items.what: Older library for testing trading strategies.

items.name: Prophet
items.what: Forecasts time series with trends and seasons.
items.fit: Tempting for 'predict the ETF', but markets are not seasonal patterns.
items.note: Would give confident-looking but unreliable price forecasts; that is why this dashboard shows ranges instead.

items.name: FinRL
items.fit: Research toy, not for long-term investing.
items.note: No reliable evidence it beats simple investing after costs.

items.name: AI Hedge Fund
items.what: Experiment where AI agents discuss stocks.
items.note: High stars reflect hype. The project itself is a learning demo.
